items.kind: bug (steer leads to a silent no-op; S) — B528's residual
items.title: a WHOLE write to a bare `is` capture (`if held is Some(let v) { v += 1; }`) still steers to `mut`, and `Some(mut v)` then compiles and the write does not reach `held` — B528's steer was rewritten for writes INTO a capture and for every `match` leg capture, not for an `is` capture's own rebind
items.body: B528's new refusal ("it is a COPY of the payload the pattern takes out of `held` … match a view of it, `match &mut held`") is withheld from a whole assignment to an `is` capture because a guard's continuation binding (`if !(x is Some(let n)) { panic(..) } n = 5;`, B222/B237) is an ordinary local whose rebind `mut` answers. The scalar `is` capture inside the guarded block is the same shape and the same trap. Rec: tell the two apart by where the capture is visible (the guarded block vs the continuation) and give the block's capture B528's steer. Sizing S.

items.title: under `match &mut place`, a capture inside a TUPLE sub-pattern (`Some((let a, let b))`) is still a copy: a write to it is refused with the old `declare it mut` steer, and `mut a` is accepted and its write does not land — the payload-view rule binds captures through variant payloads only
items.discussion: solver-c-46 (Order 46), building B509 (payload-views.md §3 A says every `let` capture of the match is a view)
items.body: Tuples store flat, so a tuple-typed leaf inside a tuple pattern is a reslice (`subject.slice(..)`), which cannot be a view; a one-slot leaf could be the `(tuple, offset)` pair. B509 S1 excluded tuple sub-patterns entirely, and the Q4 refusal (`mut` capture under a view subject) covers only the payload-view positions, so the trap B528 closed survives one pattern level down. Rec: one-slot tuple leaves become views (JS pair / native binding modes already give `&mut`), a multi-slot tuple leaf is refused under a view subject with a steer to bind the tuple whole; extend Q4 to every capture under a view subject. Sizing S–M.

items.title: B495's mode-mismatch refusal ("this closure takes `str` by value where its type takes a view `&str` … `\|c\| f(*c)`") carries no quick-fix data: offer the literal's parameter rewritten to the type's mode when the literal is right there, or the adapter `\|c\| f(*c)` / `\|c\| f(&c)` when it is not
items.discussion: solver-c-46 (Order 46); closure-type-views.md §4 asks for the quick fix, S3
items.body: The refusal is built in `closure_mode_mismatch_message` (analyzer) and reaches every mismatch site through `type_mismatch_message`; the parameter index and both modes are known there. Rec: a `ClosureModeFix { span, replacement }` beside the message in the style of `parsing::foreign_spelling_fix`, read by the LSP's code-action table. Sizing S; vilan-core + vilan-lsp.
